tools.name: preparation_status
tools.description: Read product and architecture stages, exact revisions, operator feedback and linked development. Available before project setup.

tools.name: preparation_create
tools.description: Create a product change. Product and architecture require explicit operator decisions in the web panel before development.

tools.name: preparation_activate
tools.description: Select the change for subsequent development tasks. Does not approve any stage.

tools.name: preparation_quick
tools.description: Start a quick change to one existing npm or pnpm repository from a short instruction and one observable result. The same requestKey returns the change it created; another payload under it is refused. Product and architecture stay operator-approved revisions (compact ones are fine); nothing is approved by this call.

tools.name: preparation_setup
tools.description: Propose what setup will apply to a quick change: a profile (npm-project or pnpm-project for an existing repository) and, when the repository has its own check commands, the gates that run them (a test gate needs a JUnit report). The panel shows the files setup would create, keep or refuse before anything is written; setup --change applies exactly the latest proposal.

tools.name: preparation_expand
tools.description: Move a quick change to the full route when it needs several components or dependent tasks. Keeps the instruction, criterion and all revisions; explain why.

tools.name: preparation_product
tools.description: Save a new immutable product draft with optimistic concurrency: personas with goals and pains, releases as the scope boundary, and features whose scenarios name a persona and whose acceptance criteria name a release. Resolve ambiguity the way the relevant persona would. Never approves it; a revision invalidates the prior architecture for new work.

tools.name: preparation_architecture
tools.description: Save architecture, justified stack and structured C1/C2 only after operator product approval. Does not approve development.

tools.name: preparation_references
tools.description: Save the first design step: candidate references with the property taken from each and an optional screenshot stored beside them. The operator accepts or rejects each one. A change that touches no interface sets applicable=false with a reason, which ends the design track.

tools.name: preparation_concept
tools.description: Save the second design step after the operator approved the references: the concept and the rendered sketches they choose between. Sketches are files or links, one of them marked accepted.

tools.name: preparation_design
tools.description: Save the third design step after the operator approved the concept: the palette, semantic tokens, guidelines, what is shared and what differs per channel, and the handoff package. Screen layouts stay per-feature UI contracts inside development.

tools.name: preparation_submit
tools.description: Validate the current draft and send it to the operator for approval. Unresolved questions or incomplete C1/C2 block submission.

tools.name: preparation_progress
tools.description: Append a short note about the work in progress so the panel shows the session is active before any revision exists. Context only; never approves or reports evidence.

tools.name: preparation_question
tools.description: Record open product or architecture questions for the operator, or withdraw ones that no longer apply. The operator answers them in the panel; an answered question cannot be withdrawn.

tools.name: preparation_resolve
tools.description: Record a decision with its rationale in the durable journal, optionally closing an answered question, or withdraw decisions that no longer hold. Does not approve a stage.

tools.name: intent_render
tools.description: Render component intent from committed REQ sources, or a workspace product/application/feature map with pinned local story references. Returns Markdown only; does not write, approve or commit it.

tools.name: intent_snapshot
tools.description: Read the committed intent source returned for the selected owner (docs/implementation-intent.md in embedded mode, otherwise INTENT.md) and exact story REQ bindings. Add a configured test gate/scenario, and bind the detailed requirements too.

tools.name: intent_report
tools.description: Audit all release stories and REQ sources. Product maps add application/feature progress and current bound ChangeSet acceptance. Read-only; never accepts a release or copies local task text.

tools.name: product_view
tools.description: Read the committed product/application/component map and computed feature progress for a release. Includes explicit deferred/not-applicable scope and joint verification. No writes or model calls.

tools.name: memory_retain
tools.description: Save an immutable, source-pinned statement in its Git owner. References are local. This is context, never approval or evidence.

tools.name: memory_recall
tools.description: Retrieve owner-local knowledge within a byte budget, excluding stale/conflicting statements and hypotheses by default. No model calls.

tools.name: discussion_read
tools.description: Read a task discussion page in seq order: forward from cursor (the last seq returned; follow nextCursor), or backward with latest: true or before: <seq> (follow previousCursor). version is the thread version for writes. Notes, change requests and their dispositions are local history of the task owner: they never change the task, its approvals, queue or attempts, and Git sync does not carry them.

tools.name: discussion_post
tools.description: Post a note or a change request to a task discussion as the lead. Needs idempotencyKey (a repeat returns the same message, another payload under it is refused) and expectedVersion (the thread version you read; a mismatch is 409 — re-read). Text: up to 16 KiB UTF-8, no control characters other than newline and tab; the reply carries an excerpt of long text. supersedes corrects your own latest version of a message. A change request does not alter an approved or accepted task: apply it through a new revision. kind answer answers a writer question: input {requestId, expectedVersion (the request version, which is the check instead of the thread version), optionId?, kind?}; the lead rule of input_answer applies, the answer text lives once in the request and the message links its revision; an answer to a question already cancelled or superseded is kept as discussion history (input.accepted false) and resumes nothing; an applied answer is not corrected (409).

tools.name: discussion_resolve
tools.description: Record how a change request was handled: accepted (refs to the board revision or tasks created after the request, or to a draft task edited after it, alone or with its unaccepted revision), rejected with a reason, or needs-answer (the operator answers in the panel and the request returns to discussion_inbox). Only the latest version of a request is handled; accepted and rejected are final. expectedVersion is the thread version from discussion_inbox. Reading a request is not handling it.

tools.name: discussion_inbox
tools.description: List change requests waiting for the lead across tasks, oldest event first: the latest version of each request without a disposition, or answered by the operator after needs-answer (reopened). Each new operator answer is a new event: the request may appear again, later in the order, even on a later page of the same pass. Each entry is bounded: an excerpt, textBytes, truncated and the thread version for discussion_resolve; read the full text with discussion_read. Follow nextCursor.

tools.name: usage_report
tools.description: Read paginated owner-local invocation costs (USD amounts are API-equivalent estimates — reported by the CLI or computed from prices — not subscription charges), versions and telemetry coverage; never evidence. With repositoryId: that component. Without it: the workspace contour (planning, answer review); in an embedded workspace also its component. scope.owners names the owners read; each record carries owner (@workspace for the contour).

tools.name: decision_report
tools.description: Read recorded dispatch inputs and observed outcomes. Other component tasks appear only as dependency IDs.

tools.name: strategy_replay
tools.description: Audit a fixed strategy against prefix-only dispatch inputs. Unobserved alternatives stay unsupported; no policy is installed.

tools.name: signal_ingest
tools.description: Record a normalized external observation in its component, deduplicate it and propose draft work or a correction. A resolved signal never supplies test evidence or accepts work.

tools.name: signal_status
tools.description: Read external signal receipts in one component. No remote requests or model calls.

tools.name: workflow_start
tools.description: Enqueue idempotent board review, execution and acceptance or ChangeSet verification. A running server may invoke models. Operator policy remains enforced.

tools.name: workflow_status
tools.description: Read owner-local durable stage jobs, the queue stop and running attempts and checks without movement (liveness and operations: quiet or stalled, idle time, activity, next step). No model calls or execution leases are granted.

tools.name: workflow_retry
tools.description: Retry a diagnosed failed stage within its original attempt budget. Never retries failed task implementations automatically.

tools.name: workflow_metrics
tools.description: Read per-owner execution measurements, incomplete attempts and unknown cost. USD amounts and budgets are API-equivalent estimates, not subscription charges; the workspace budget counts lifetime workspace spend. No model calls.

tools.name: value_report
tools.description: Read the effect report: accepted tasks, first try, sent back by checks/review, approval-to-merge time, known spend per accepted task (API-equivalent estimate), environment failures and recorded interventions. Omit repositoryId for the whole workspace. Bounds are explicit: "lower" means at least, a range means unknown inputs, null/unknown is never zero; under 20 no percentages, under 5 no medians. JSON only; summary detail omits per-task rows and evidence links (the CLI report has them). Read-only, no model calls.

tools.name: session_handoff
tools.description: Read the context handoff pack for a new lead session; start every new lead session with it instead of recalling the previous one. One store snapshot: task counts and limits, queue pause and who lifts it, controller, running and unfinished attempts, open tasks with their next step, stops and decisions awaiting the lead or user, recent failures, budgets and the next step of the board. Board lead workflow jobs count as the graph jobs: their repairs and planned retries are in the pack. next.command names harness CLI commands, never run them; host.next is the DevContour step decided from state by the rules of the lead job loop (also when the running server holds the controller role), with host.next.loop saying what the loop does next: wait for a live job (including one that lifts the queue pause), decide when the loop would stop the job (repair budget or failure class: fix or retry the task by hand first) or the attempts of the job are spent, workflow_retry {key, repositoryId} for a failed job a retry would move on, workflow_start for a board with an approved plan and no job for its current input, decide with decision plan for a board whose plan is not approved (draft tasks: choose the scope, e.g. review-plan --tasks, never workflow_start for the whole plan), fix-input when workflow_start would be refused, queue_set for an operator pause no job lifts, operator in approvalMode operator. For a writer question: answer-input when a blocking question waits for an answer (the lead answers with input_answer only when no floor applies and approvalMode is agent; otherwise wait for the operator in the panel), apply-input when a saved answer is not applied or went stale (input_context, input_review, input_target, input_apply; a rejected review is corrected first) or, with code apply-carry, when the answer of a superseded question waits to be carried into its task (params.order: draft — carry while the task is a draft, then approve; unreleased — pause, approve, carry, lift the pause; now — carry before the next attempt; only a carry the engine would allow now, into a task neither cancelled nor done; while attempts run on its board the step is wait with params.active, and the chain starts after they end; for an approved task while the queue runs or its pause is one a job loop lifts, it is first queue_set with params.pause, since the queue would issue the task without the answer; a waiting carry ranks like wait, and on the plan path a failed job of another board comes before it), close-follow-up for an open non-blocking follow-up (input_cancel to accept the assumption, or correct the board and input_supersede). host.next has a stable code and params (only what its other fields lack); detail is its text in the hintLocale language of the config (English when unset), commands and JSON verbatim. When pack.next is a lead or user decision outside the queue, host.next invents no queue step (workflow_start, queue_set), only steps of that board: wait for its live job when the job loop acts next (a loop that only waits for tasks does not hide the decision), workflow_retry of its failed job, or a job or plan decision. repairs lists live jobs first, then jobs for the current input, then newest first. Omit boardId for the whole workspace. host.discussion lists up to five unresolved requests to the lead from task discussions as redacted excerpts (the rest via discussion_inbox with nextCursor, full text via discussion_read; omitted when none fit the response limit); resolve each with discussion_resolve. intentions are your own notes, the only text not from the store: trimmed, empty ones dropped, at most 20 non-empty, longer than 1000 chars clipped and counted in truncated. format md returns the same pack as Markdown. Over the response limit, entries are dropped in the pack order and counted in truncated (bySize), and full names the CLI that prints the whole pack. Not the ChangeSet delivery handoff (devcontour handoff --changeset). Read-only, no model calls.

tools.name: requirements_snapshot
tools.description: Read REQ sections from committed repository HEAD. Bind returned digest/text to a task and a configured test gate.

tools.name: requirements_report
tools.description: Compare current requirement sections with task evidence. Historical done is unchanged; stale requirements are not current coverage. Returns a summary over all tasks of the component (tasks, requirements, stale, counts by proof level) and task rows within the response limit: without cursor and limit the whole list when it fits, otherwise one page (limit, default 50, max 200); pass nextCursor as cursor for the next page. complete is true only when tasks holds the whole report. A task whose requirements alone exceed the page lists omittedRequirements. full names the CLI command that prints the whole report. Read-only, no model calls.

tools.name: requirements_correct
tools.description: Create draft replacements for changed requirements on an accepted board. Preserve history and require new plan review.

tools.name: project_context
tools.description: Read workspace identity, components, modes and supported operations. Does not start work.

tools.name: project_overview
tools.description: Read bounded summaries of the common workspace or one repository; follow nextCursor.

tools.name: task_briefing
tools.description: Read all pages of the task requirements, contracts, execution policy and blocking reasons. Optional repositoryId (multi-repository workspace): the task must belong to that component, otherwise the call is refused.

tools.name: checkpoint_save
tools.description: Save an immutable Git-portable context note in the selected owner, requiring the current overview revision. This does not approve work.

tools.name: checkpoint_changes
tools.description: Compare current records with an owner-local checkpoint. Notes are historical context, not instructions or evidence.

tools.name: plan_import
tools.description: Import a draft task DAG. Without boardId it opens a new board; with boardId of an accepted board it opens the next stage as that board's next revision, so one release stays on one board. In a product change, imported tasks are bound to changeId when given, otherwise to the change of the board's tasks (next stage), otherwise to the active change; the response names changeId. This does not approve the plan or execute agents. Do not blindly retry creation after an uncertain response.

tools.name: board_create
tools.description: Create a draft board in the selected repository or common workspace.

tools.name: task_create
tools.description: Add a draft task to an active board; DAG and component ownership are validated. In a product change the task is bound to task.preparation.changeId when given (changeId alone is enough; supplied digests must equal the current approved ones), otherwise to the change of the board's tasks, otherwise to the active change; a change other than that of the board's live tasks is refused; the response names the binding. An accepted board takes no tasks: open the next stage with plan_import and its boardId; board_correct only changes accepted results.

tools.name: task_edit
tools.description: Edit a draft task using the specDigest read from task_briefing. Stale edits are rejected. task.preparation.changeId rebinds the task to that product change (changeId alone is enough; stale supplied digests are refused, as is a change other than that of the board's other live tasks); without it the task keeps its own change. The response names the binding.

tools.name: task_retry
tools.description: Explicitly retry a failed or cancelled task within the attempt budget. Diagnose the failure first.

tools.name: task_assign
tools.description: Assign a task to a team member. Assignment is not a distributed lease.

tools.name: task_story
tools.description: Bind done tasks to an INTENT story without changing their approved spec, when they link the story's detailed REQs but not REQ-intent-<story>. Every detailed REQ of each task must be in that story's criteria; the story digest is pinned from committed HEAD and a reason is journaled. intent_report marks these tasks boundAfterAcceptance: the story text was not in the author's prompt. Drafts get the REQ-intent link in requirements instead.

tools.name: board_correct
tools.description: Create a correction after board acceptance, preserving history and recalculating transitive impact.

tools.name: changeset_create
tools.description: Declare a shared change across boards. Set releaseId to bind product release acceptance to the workspace INTENT map and mandatory joint tests. Verification and acceptance remain separate operations.

tools.name: queue_set
tools.description: Pause or resume issuance of tasks. Resuming may invoke configured models in a running server; this does not launch a server or cancel active runs.

tools.name: preview_status
tools.description: Read the local preview: which verified release serves the URL, its states (built, deployed, healthy, confirmed or unconfirmed), and past deployments with their errors. Deploying and rolling back are separate controlled actions through the CLI or panel.

tools.name: feasibility_spike
tools.description: Run a bounded feasibility experiment before implementation: the given argv of an oracle or prototype at a pinned commit, per input size (DEVCONTOUR_SPIKE_SIZE) and seed, under a time limit. Stores commands, versions, times, outcome and limits of inference. A timeout is inconclusive for that method and budget; it never proves hardness or permits weakening a requirement.

tools.name: feasibility_spikes
tools.description: Read stored feasibility experiments of a component with their outcome, versions and limits of inference. No commands run.

tools.name: checks_view
tools.description: Read the check contract of a task: effective check version, declared properties and actual coverage of the last gates, confirmed/proposed/disputed corpus cases (paginated with cursor), failure history by property, the recovery episode, remaining budgets and the next step with who must act. Read-only; starts nothing.

tools.name: checks_case_submit
tools.description: Submit a concrete input for a declared property. The controller runs the pinned oracle and the implementation on the defective commit twice; only a reproducible discrepancy becomes an immutable corpus version adopted by the listed unfinished tasks (waiting for an active run). Wrong expectations are refuted, timeouts inconclusive; nothing in the input or a reproduction command is executed. Idempotent by key. Removal, replaced expectations, tolerance, checker or command changes are refused: use contract-change.

tools.name: checks_adopt
tools.description: Adopt an existing corpus version by explicitly listed unfinished tasks of the same check contract. Waits for active runs and holds their issuance; accepted tasks are never changed.

tools.name: recovery_decide
tools.description: Record the lead decision for a recovery episode (two failures on one property) with the expected record version: add confirmed cases under the pinned oracle, one retry with a new hypothesis, a proposal for normal review (strengthen checker, split task), a product conflict for the user, or an environment stop. Never resets attempts.

tools.name: contract_change_status
tools.description: Read a contract-change operation: its step, holds, history, earlier redactions and the next step. Read-only.

tools.name: contract_change_revise
tools.description: Revise a failed, stale or waiting contract change to the current committed redaction with the expected record version. An optional proposal replaces the stored one for the same contract (same file or inline title, repositoryId and component) — new text, artifacts, checks, underTest — after the start pre-checks (artifact pinning, import closure, check declaration) and before any model call. Before side effects the same operation is re-reviewed with its holds and history kept; after them a linked successor takes the holds over. Effects are never rolled back.

tools.name: input_list
tools.description: List writer questions (input requests) with state, severity, floors, version and who acts next: awaiting-answer, answer-saved, context-review, review-rejected (the reviewer rejected the answer), ready-to-apply, applied-awaiting-claim, delivered (only after the writer call with the answer started), stale, cancelled, superseded. No question or answer text. Read-only.

tools.name: input_show
tools.description: Read one writer question: question, options, recommended option, severity and floors, draft files, the latest answer in full, earlier answers as digest and excerpt, review rounds, target and delivery. Read-only.

tools.name: input_answer
tools.description: Answer a writer question with the expected request version. The lead may answer only a question without floors in approvalMode agent; otherwise the operator answers in the panel. A requirement-change answer is not continued: reopen and respecify the task within the write scope of its role (paths of another role need a separate task of that role), input_supersede with the same task, carry the answer while the task is a draft, then approve the task; the approval keeps the carried answer when the spec is unchanged after the carry. Does not resume the task.

tools.name: input_context
tools.description: Build the immutable context snapshot with the latest answer (the effective task snapshot plus input/<id>.md and its manifest) and store it by digest. The manifest lists the discussion messages that recorded the answers and the messageIds you select (id, seq, digest; their text is not added). Not activated; idempotent per digest.

tools.name: input_review
tools.description: Review the answer snapshot with the plan reviewer (round subject input-<id>): approve only if the answer clarifies without changing the approved spec; the reviewer sees the write scope of the role. Refused before the model call when the snapshot is missing or does not carry the latest answer, and for a carry whose task writePaths lie outside the write scope of the role (409 ROLE_SCOPE). Approval does not activate anything. When attempts of the task board are running, the result carries warning and activeAttempts: input_apply waits for them (applied: false with active).

tools.name: input_target
tools.description: Propose the continuation target for a reviewed answer snapshot (or the carry target of a superseded question) and list why applying would be refused now, including carry writePaths outside the role write scope and a board not yet released (all tasks drafts). Read-only.

tools.name: input_apply
tools.description: Apply the answer in one transaction with the exact request version, answer digest, snapshot and target digest: activates the snapshot for the task and requeues it. In approvalMode operator the operator applies in the panel. Busy graph attempts or exhausted limits return applied=false with the reason; the answer stays.

tools.name: input_cancel
tools.description: Cancel a writer question with the expected version and a reason; also closes follow-ups (assumption accepted). A blocking question follows the answer rule: floored or approvalMode operator questions are cancelled by the operator.

tools.name: input_supersede
tools.description: Supersede a writer question once the spec of its task has changed: reopen and respecify the task, then supersede with the same task and carry the answer (input_context, input_review, input_target, input_apply) while the task is a draft, then approve it: the approval keeps the carried answer when the spec is unchanged after the carry. A superseded question does not hold the task, so a carry after the approval needs a queue pause. The result nextStep names the order. Refused with 409 SPEC_UNCHANGED while the spec is unchanged; a blocking question the lead may not answer is superseded by the operator (403 OPERATOR_ANSWERS). The old task is not resumed by a requirement change without carry. A non-blocking follow-up may also be superseded by a newer task of the same board, for example the replacement created by board_correct.

tools.name: attention_list
tools.description: List the attention center: one ordered list of current items that need someone to act, from the same source rules as the panel (preparation questions and stage reviews, writer questions, stopped tasks, lead job decisions, discussion requests, pauses, waits, budgets, contract changes, ChangeSet acceptance, preview problems, stalls). Default actor lead; each item has sourceKey, occurrenceId, sourceVersion, category, actor, reason, impact (covered tasks and the tasks waiting on them), subject and since. A cascade is one root item. Links open the panel at the subject (task list, the stage of the question, the discussion message). Operator domain actions carry the full question (prompt) and answer choices. Reading is not handling: act through the source operation (preparation_*, discussion_*, input_*, task_retry, workflow_*). Read-only; operator read marks are not included. Available before setup.
